title: Heading with Partial Emphasis

illustrates.quote: Do not use typeform to indicate specific print attributes such as italics, boldface, and font style/size for print headings unless it is necessary for clarity.

blocks.features: Centered heading combining an author name in plain serif and an italicised work title; only the play title "A Doll's House" is italicised in print, the author name is not.

blocks.text: Nora *(pause)* Does anything strike you as we sit here?
blocks.features: Plain body text; stage direction '(pause)' is italicised in print.

print.notes: Illustrates that print italics within a heading (here, only the play title, not the author name) are ignored in braille except where needed for distinction -- the whole heading is rendered without added typeform emphasis except on the title, per the exception in rule 4.3.7.
print.printFeatures: Centered bold blue heading combining an unitalicised author name and an italicised work title; body paragraph below with an italicised parenthetical stage direction.

braille.notes: Line 1 blank; line 2 the centered heading, with the title portion "A Doll's House" wrapped in a typeform (italics) indicator pair -- the one retained font attribute, needed to distinguish the title from the author's name -- while 'Henrik Ibsen,' carries no such indicator; line 3 blank; lines 4-5 the dialogue paragraph.

uncertain: The paragraph's exact final word(s) (line 5, 'we sit ...') are approximated from the braille contractions alone (no clean PDF/print image reading was available for this literary excerpt's exact wording); the heading text and its italics placement -- this example's actual point -- are not in doubt.

Even with the heading's *italic* markup correctly marking “A Doll's House” per rule 4.3.7's clarity exception, Emboss's formatHeading unconditionally strips typeform from every heading and has no way to invoke that exception -- see standards-findings.md F-41. Expect the gold braille's italic brackets around the title to be absent from Emboss's actual output; this is a documented Emboss gap, not a gold-file error.
resolution: braille.lines agree; wording merged. Heading centered (level 1), confirmed by the centering-formula check (indent 3 matches (40-34)/2). print.blocks text corrected during model-building verification: the heading needs *italic* markup on "A Doll's House" (the one retained font attribute per rule 4.3.7's exception) to produce the expected typeform brackets, and the paragraph's stage direction needs *(pause)* markup, not the literal BRF ASCII quotation glyphs that had been pasted into the print text by mistake.
